content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

Section 6.3 of the Transfer and Servicing Agreement contains a genuine counterparty-side indemnity running in our favour:

- **Who is bound:** Cellco, both as Servicer (expressly including in its capacity as Custodian) and as Marketing Agent.
- **Beneficiaries:** the Issuer, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee (including as Note Paying Agent) and their officers, directors, employees and agents.
- **Scope:** all fees, expenses, losses, claims, actions, suits, damages and liabilities (including reasonable legal fees), i.e. third-party proceedings as well as direct loss, resulting from Cellco's willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence — the rule's "own misconduct" limb.
- **Procedure:** prompt notice that is not a condition to recovery absent prejudice, defence assumed at Cellco's expense with counsel reasonably satisfactory to the Indemnified Person, separate counsel funded on conflict, and no settlement implying acknowledgement without consent. Section 6.3(c) survives resignation, termination and trustee removal; 6.3(d) is only a customary repayment-on-double-recovery mechanic.
- **No cap and no reverse indemnity:** the indemnity is uncapped (better than the fallback's 3× super-cap), and neither the Issuer nor the Depositor gives any indemnity to Cellco anywhere in the agreement, so the walk-away scenario (one-way customer indemnity) does not arise.

Noted in the rationale rather than flagged: there is no IP-infringement limb, which is immaterial in this securitisation context (no vendor deliverables or IP grant), and the Depositor is not itself an "Indemnified Person" under Section 6.3(a), consistent with its recourse sitting in the originator/transfer documents.
